entries.metric: CMOSE · subjects appearing in >1 official split
entries.caveat: CMOSE's released split assigns clips, not subjects. The same person, webcam and session therefore appear in train and test. This is not a defect of the dataset — the paper reports a random segment split — but any number computed under it measures something weaker than subject-level generalisation.

Single permitted run under a pre-registered protocol; the protocol is now closed. Validation R@1 was 0.6343, so test exceeds validation by 0.0119.

entries.metric: Branch A · ablation Δ R@1 (Hungarian − ordinal)
entries.caveat: Identical frames, captions, boxes, schedule, LR and seed; only the unit→box binding differs. R@10 differs by only 0.014, so the gain is attribution, not detection.

entries.metric: Branch A · ablation Δ R@1 (p≥0.9 filter − unfiltered Hungarian)
entries.caveat: NEGATIVE result: the confidence filter does not help. Retains 90.3% of the Hungarian gain on 59.7% of the training regions.
CITE THIS, NOT 0.9231. The 92.3% figure used spatial_weight=0.5, whose spatial term leaks the ground-truth left-to-right ordering.
DO NOT CITE. spatial_weight=0.5 feeds the ground-truth ordering into the cost matrix.

entries.metric: teacher frame agreement with human gold
entries.caveat: Empirical teacher benchmark, NOT a theoretical ceiling. Corroborated by the disjoint scattered sample's 85.9%.
Weakest field: activity, 78.9%.
Barely above chance (0.5). MEASURED LIMITATION: the 7 basic Ekman expressions do not deliver academic-emotion (Pekrun) recognition. The thesis must not claim boredom detection.

p<0.0001 by 5,000-permutation test, and the sign is REVERSED versus the naive hypothesis. Weak correlation. Evidence that cue meaning is setting-dependent — the strongest support for the visible-cue framing.

DO NOT CITE as a validation result. p=0.74; the model predicts off-task on 0–17% of DIPSER frames because the geometry features are far out of distribution. Measures domain shift, not the cue↔engagement link.

DO NOT CITE as a transfer score. SCB annotates ONLY behaviour-exhibiting students, so correctly detecting an ordinary seated student scores as a false positive; and the label mapping (BowHead→'sleeping head down') is semantically wrong for a lecture hall. Report as a qualitative limitation. The least-confounded number is localisation recall 0.392.
DO NOT CITE. Computed on one rank's shard, not the full validation set. Under correct measurement the 556/570 ordering reverses.

entries.split: validation on the sequence builder's own 102/25 split
entries.caveat: Superseded. Correct as far as it goes, but (a) it is a VALIDATION number on a split with no test set, (b) single seed, (c) no confidence interval, (d) checkpoint selected by argmax over a metric that swings ±0.05 between epochs. Use the thesis_eval ladder instead.
Single A100, batched CLIP. Detector is a fixed ~122 ms of the ~140 ms frame budget. Describe the system as NEAR-real-time; 7.1 FPS does not meet a 25 fps camera rate.
Scaling limitation: per-student feature extraction dominates beyond ~10 students.
